questions.question: In August 1907, Madam Bhikaji Cama became the first person to hoist Indian flag on foreign soil in:
questions.solution:
In August 1907, Madam Bhikaji Cama became the first person to hoist the Indian flag on foreign soil in Stuttgart, Germany.
  • She is known as the 'Mother of Indian Revolution'.
  • The flag she hoisted was a modification of the 'Calcutta Flag'.

questions.question: The Bahamani Sultanate was founded by which of the following leaders?
questions.solution:
The Bahamani Sultanate was founded by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (also known as Zafar Khan) in 1347.
  • The capital was initially Gulbarga and later shifted to Bidar.
  • It was the first independent Muslim kingdom in South India.

questions.question: The rulers of which of the following dynasties built the Khajuraho temples between 950 to 1050 A.D in the central India?
questions.solution:
The Khajuraho Temples were built by the Chandela Dynasty between 950 and 1050 AD.
  • These temples are famous for their Nagara-style architecture and erotic sculptures.
  • They are located in Madhya Pradesh and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: The Battle of Buxar was fought between the forces under the command of the British East India Company led by Hector Munro, and the combined armies of______.
questions.option_1: Mir Qasim, Mughal Emperor Shah Alam & Shuja-ud-daulah of Awadh
questions.option_2: Mir jafar, Siraj-ud-Daulah and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II
questions.option_3: Mir Jafar, Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah II, Shuja-ud-Daulah
questions.option_4: Siraj-ud-Daulah, Shuja-ud-Daulah, Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II
questions.solution:
The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought between the British EIC (Hector Munro) and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shah Alam II, and Shuja-ud-daulah.
  • This victory led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).
  • It established the British as the masters of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.

questions.question: With reference to the Land Revenue System of Mughal Empire, the term ‘_________’ was the amount assessed.
questions.solution:
In the Mughal Land Revenue System, 'Jama' referred to the assessed amount of revenue, while 'Hasil' was the actual amount collected.
  • Land was classified into four types: Polaj, Parauti, Chachar, and Banjar.
  • Zabit was the system of measurement used for assessment.

questions.question: Who among the following Governor Generals enacted the law against the Sati practice in December 1829?
questions.solution:
Lord William Bentinck enacted the Sati Regulation Act in December 1829, making the practice of Sati illegal and punishable.
  • He was strongly supported by the Indian reformer Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
  • Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the ‘Asiatic Society of Bengal’ in 1784?
questions.solution:
The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded by Sir William Jones in 1784.
  • The objective was to encourage Oriental studies and research on Indian history and culture.
  • Warren Hastings was the Governor-General during its establishment.

questions.question: Who among the following organised the armed rebellion against the British Raj in 1879 in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
Vasudev Balwant Phadke, known as the 'Father of Indian Armed Rebellion', organized an armed revolt against the British in 1879.
  • He formed a revolutionary group called the Ramoshi Peasant Force.
  • He aimed to create an Indian Republic by overthrowing British rule.

questions.question: At which of the following places was the formal proclamation of the Swadeshi movement made on 7 August 1905?
questions.solution:
The formal proclamation of the Swadeshi Movement was made on 7 August 1905 at the Calcutta Town Hall.
  • The movement was a reaction to the Partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon.
  • It emphasized the boycott of British goods and the use of Indian products.

questions.question: Mahadev Govind Ranade was primarily associated with the:
questions.solution:
Mahadev Govind Ranade was a key leader of the Prarthana Samaj.
  • He is known as the 'Socrates of Maharashtra' and was a mentor to Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
  • He also founded the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian state was the first to sign subsidiary alliance with the British?
questions.solution:
The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to sign the Subsidiary Alliance with the British in 1798.
  • The policy was introduced by Lord Wellesley to expand British influence.
  • Under this, the Indian ruler had to maintain British troops at their own cost.

questions.question: The Battle of Tukaroi also known as the Battle of Bajhaura or the Battle of Mughulmar was fought between the Mughal Empire and the Bengal Sultanate in which of the following year______?
questions.solution:
The Battle of Tukaroi was fought in 1575 between the Mughal Empire (under Akbar) and the Bengal Sultanate (under Daud Khan Karrani).
  • The Mughals won, leading to the annexation of Bengal and Bihar.
  • It is also known as the Battle of Mughulmar.

questions.question: The Kadamba Dynasty was an ancient royal dynasty of the modern day:
questions.solution:
The Kadamba Dynasty (345–525 CE) was an ancient royal dynasty that ruled from Banavasi in modern-day Karnataka.
  • It was founded by Mayurasharma.
  • They were the first to use Kannada as an official administrative language.

questions.question: In which year did Ambedkar start a temple entry movement?
questions.solution:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar started a temple entry movement in 1927, specifically the Mahad Satyagraha to allow Dalits to use water from public tanks.
  • In 1930, he led the famous Kalaram Temple entry movement in Nashik.
  • These movements aimed at challenging caste discrimination.

questions.question: Which of the following tax was taken not in cash but in the form of forced labour in Chola empire?
questions.solution:
In the Chola Empire, 'Vetti' was a tax taken in the form of forced labour.
  • 'Kadamai' was the term used for land revenue.
  • The Cholas were known for their highly efficient local self-government system.

questions.question: Which Gharana was propounded by Bade Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh Jarnail Khan?
questions.solution:
The Patiala Gharana was propounded by Bade Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh Jarnail Khan.
  • It is one of the most prominent Vocal Gharanas of Hindustani classical music.
  • It is famous for its Thumri and Khayal singing styles.

questions.question: When was Awadh annexed by Lord Dalhousie?
questions.solution:
Awadh was annexed by Lord Dalhousie in 1856 on the grounds of 'internal misgovernance'.
  • The Nawab of Awadh at that time was Wajid Ali Shah.
  • This annexation was a major cause of the Revolt of 1857.

questions.question: Vijayanagara empire was founded in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by two brothers, Harihara I and Bukka Raya I.
  • The capital was Hampi, located on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.
  • The empire reached its peak under Krishnadevaraya.

questions.question: Bijapur was annexed by Aurangzeb in which year?
questions.solution:
The Sultanate of Bijapur was annexed by the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in 1686 (Note: Option 3 is 1685).
  • Bijapur was ruled by the Adil Shahi dynasty.
  • Aurangzeb also annexed Golconda in 1687.

questions.question: Who among the following is credited with popularising the catchphrase ‘Inquilab Zindabad’?
questions.solution:
The slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' (Long Live the Revolution) was popularized by Bhagat Singh.
  • It was originally coined by the Urdu poet and freedom fighter Hasrat Mohani in 1921.
  • Bhagat Singh used it after throwing a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929.

questions.question: The Battle of Khatoli fought was in 1517 between the kingdom of Mewar under Rana Sanga and ______.
questions.solution:
The Battle of Khatoli (1517) was fought between Rana Sanga of Mewar and Ibrahim Lodi.
  • Rana Sanga emerged victorious in this battle.
  • This conflict weakened the Lodi Dynasty before the Mughal invasion.

questions.question: In which of the following sessions did the congress split into two factions?
questions.solution:
The Indian National Congress split into two factions (Moderates and Extremists) during the Surat Session of 1907.
  • The session was presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh.
  • The two groups reunited later in the Lucknow Session of 1916.

questions.question: The Rolling plan was implemented between which two five-year plans?
questions.solution:
The Rolling Plan was implemented between the Fifth and Sixth Five-Year Plans (1978–1980).
  • It was introduced by the Janata Party government led by Morarji Desai.
  • It was discarded when the Congress government returned to power in 1980.

questions.question: The All-India Khilafat Conference in November 1919 took place at:
questions.solution:
The All-India Khilafat Conference was held in Delhi in November 1919.
  • Mahatma Gandhi was elected as its President.
  • The Khilafat movement aimed to protect the Caliphate in Turkey.

questions.question: Revolutionary hero Ashfaqulla Khan was sentenced to death for _________________.
questions.option_1: burning of the Chauri Chaura police station
questions.solution:
Ashfaqulla Khan was sentenced to death for his role in the Kakori Train Robbery (1925).
  • He was a prominent member of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
  • He was the first Muslim to be hanged for the Indian freedom struggle.
